A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRAN-TED and TED-6K research. Their text, tables, figures, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original encoder evaluations, trained text-to-image and text-to-video results, ablations, and benchmark robustness and stability experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds encoder evaluations, downstream reward scores, and qualitative generation comparisons.

M1.justification: The contrastively trained context aggregator, Qwen3-VL fine-tuning, normalized layer weighting, and joint-training-then-freezing procedure remain unchanged. The overview's change from captioning data to VQA data aligns with the VQA procedure already described in v1 Section 3.4.

E1.justification: Section 4.2 expands downstream evaluation beyond GenAI-Bench by adding DrawBench prompts for text-to-image generation and TA-hard prompts for text-to-video generation. This substantially broadens the data supporting benchmark validation across both modalities; TED-6K and the training-data coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Llama3-8B-Instruct, InternLM3-8B-Instruct, Gemma3-4b-it, and InternVL3-9B-Instruct, substantially broadening encoder-family comparisons. Gemma3 also joins the existing text-to-image comparison in Table 3. Existing comparators are retained; newly cited methods such as ELLA are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds UnifiedReward-2 scoring on DrawBench and VideoAlign scoring on TA-hard. Correlation analyses expand from six to eight encoder configurations for images and four to five for videos. Existing training budgets, freezing schedules, resolution, and inference settings remain unchanged in v1 Appendix C.1 and v3 Appendix D.1.

E4.justification: Table 5 extends the existing fixed-weight, continuously learned-weight, and two-step ablation with UnifiedReward scores. New Appendix C provides qualitative comparisons for 21 GenAI-Bench prompts, illustrating counting, attributes, spatial relations, and negation. The existing shuffling, pooling-versus-QA, stability, and weight-dynamics analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five shuffling runs, five aggregator-training runs per tested model, maximum score variation of 0.02, and Pearson correlations with p-values. Additional correlations and changed coefficients do not introduce a different statistical procedure or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds encoder scores, reward-score columns in Tables 3-5, qualitative outputs, and updated correlations for enlarged comparison sets. Qwen3-8B last-layer GenAI performance in Table 3 changes from 71.15 to 72.42 without a stated setting change. GRAN-TED's existing TED-6K score of 57.42 and generation scores of 77.41 and 80.33 remain unchanged; the latter move from v1 Table 6 into v3 Tables 3-4.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations, including the aggregator formulation in Appendix A and spectral-bias/non-stationary-conditioning argument in Appendix B, are retained. Reformatting does not introduce a new proof, assumption, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction newly quantify evaluation efficiency as approximately 750 times faster, contrasting four minutes for TED-6K evaluation with 50 hours for diffusion-model training under the authors' setup. The central benchmark, encoder, and downstream-improvement claims retain their original scope.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies the claim that Norm-Avg uniformly beats single-layer features to say it generally does, consistent with the added InternVL3 results. It adds a proposed explanation involving thinking models' prefill representations and explicitly describes TED-6K as a diagnostic complement to output-level evaluation.

D1.justification: v3 elaborates human verification as two steps targeting confusing negatives with lexical similarity and character variations, and discloses evaluation/training timing. Existing architectural details, hyperparameters, and prompts are retained. However, the code-availability statement and repository link supplied in v1's abstract are removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning through ELLA, Deep Fusion, Playground v3, and text-encoder compression work. It distinguishes upstream encoder evaluation and adaptation from conditioning integration, compression, and final-output assessment. References supporting new encoders and reward evaluations are added, while LLM2Vec and VLM2Vec citations are removed.

P1.justification: Related work is rewritten, with localized clarifications in the introduction, method, interpretation, and conclusion. Author contact and corresponding-author information are added. The main narrative order remains intact; inserting Image Examples as Appendix C moves the existing experimental details to Appendix D.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a single-column layout with resized and repositioned figures. Table 2 is transposed, Tables 3-5 gain columns or rows, and v1 Table 6 is merged into other comparisons. A substantial image-comparison gallery is added, while the unchanged statement definitions are split across Figures 13-14.

improvement.justification: Additional encoder families and DrawBench/TA-hard evaluations reduce v1's reliance on GenAI-Bench alone and strengthen support for TED-6K's predictive value. Qualitative comparisons and the qualified Norm-Avg interpretation also improve assessability. These benefits outweigh, but are tempered by, removal of the code-access link and limited protocol detail for the new reward evaluations.
